text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- After having ruled Vienna on its own for the last 50 years, the Social Democrats have had to form a coalition for the city government. The junior coalition partner People's Party will take over three seats in the new government.
- Telecommunications Minister Rudolf Scholten said he would not approve the postal system's plans to raise local telephone call prices.
- The postal system's mobile phone unit Mobilkom Austria is looking for a strategic partner.
- Some 2,000 complaints against the new corporate income tax have been lodged with Austria's constitutional court.
- Only one percent growth is expected for Austria's industry this year. Job cuts will continue next year too.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima is taking his time looking over the offers for Creditanstalt. However, he reiterated a decision would be made by the end of the year.
- Wage talks to reopen between the metal union and employers after demonstrations by the union.
- Austria's banks are planning further cuts to already low interest rates on savings accounts.
- The new 2,000 schilling state-benefit for young mothers will only be given to families with less than 39,000 schillings income.
- Post & Telekom Austria, poised for privatisation, will have to digest at least 66 billion schillings of its debts.
- British chemical giant Courtaulds is gearing up to battle fibremaker Lenzing for market leadership in Europe.
- Investor UIAG and some partners have taken over 25 percent of crane maker Palfinger. The Salzburg-based company is planning to be listed by the year 2000.
